clue.text: Won over by commercial, say, that's to be wrapped up in the present

indicators.note: over signals that the word Won is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a commercial on TV is an advert, AD for short

indicators.note: to be wrapped up hints at the letters of say being bundled and jumbled together

explanation.surface: An advertiser wins someone over with a commercial that has to be wrapped up quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be wrapped up' is an unusual anagram signal, bundling the letters of 'say' into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean at the current time, these days, as opposed to in the past.

clue.text: Conqueror, one annexing a state

parts.note: a conqueror is a victor, one who wins
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A conquering ruler takes over a neighbouring state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'annexing' is just a link here, joining the pieces in order. VICTORIA is a state of Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria is one of the six states of Australia, in the country's south-east.

clue.text: Troops slip over wet blanket

indicators.note: over in the sense of knocked over or upset signals the letters being rearranged

explanation.surface: Soldiers slip and fall onto a soggy blanket.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet blanket is a person who spoils others' fun, a killjoy.

clue.text: Start display

definitions.meaning: to begin a journey or project

explanation.surface: The start of a display.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out is to begin a journey, or to lay goods out on show.

clue.text: When penny drops from pocket there's a shout of pain

indicators.note: drops from means the coin's letter falls out of the word for pocket

parts.note: a pouch is a small pocket or bag
P is the abbreviation for a British penny

explanation.surface: Someone yelps when a coin falls out of their pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops from' removes the P (penny) from POUCH.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of sudden hurt, like a yelp.

clue.text: In case this help might be needed

definitions.text: In case this help might be needed

parts.words: In case this help might be needed
parts.note: a legal case is a lawsuit, where those unable to pay get state-funded help

explanation.surface: Help to keep in reserve, just in case.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal aid is public funding for people who cannot afford a lawyer in a court action.

clue.text: Stop lift rising and falling

indicators.note: in a down entry, these letters read the same rising as falling

parts.note: to lift something is to pull it upward

explanation.surface: Stop the lift going up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver pulls up when bringing a vehicle to a halt.

clue.text: Renounce Frenchman, say, on the way up

parts.note: Rene is a typical French man's name

indicators.note: in a down entry, on the way up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: A Frenchman renounces his claim as he climbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To renege is to go back on a promise, to withdraw or renounce it.

clue.text: Reason to go about half-time

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: to go is to move

indicators.note: half of the word time is just its first two letters

explanation.surface: A footballer gives a reason for leaving the pitch around half-time.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'half-time' as a football interval; split, it means half of the word 'time'.
explanation.definitionFit: A motive is the reason someone has for acting a certain way.

clue.text: Bird that's trapped fish behind bars

indicators.note: behind places the fish after the bars in the answer

parts.note: bars make up a cage, so the barred enclosure is CAGE
the ling is a long-bodied sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A bird has caught a fish and is now stuck behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A cageling is a bird kept confined in a cage.

clue.text: Noticed molar is serrated

parts.note: to have noticed something is to have seen or saw it
a molar is a back tooth

explanation.surface: A dentist spots that a back tooth has a jagged edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A sawtooth edge is notched like a saw blade, that is jagged or serrated.

clue.text: Glue-on transfers waste time

indicators.note: transfers suggests the letters being moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Stick-on transfer sheets are a waste of time.
explanation.definitionFit: To lounge is to laze about idly, which is spending time without purpose.

clue.text: In a trauma I will skip the country

indicators.note: will skip signals letters jumping about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone in shock says they will skip the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Mauritania is a nation in north-west Africa on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Old European making one or two points

parts.note: one point of the compass, here North, abbreviated N
taken as written
two compass points together, South and East, giving SE

explanation.surface: An ancient Scandinavian makes one or two points in an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' does service for compass points: one point is N, two points are SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Norseman was an ancient Scandinavian, a person from early northern Europe.

clue.text: Sort of diet that is less stiff

definitions.text: Sort of diet that is less stiff

parts.words: Sort of diet that is less stiff
parts.note: starch stiffens laundry, so cutting it makes collars less stiff; it is also a carbohydrate cut in a slimming diet

explanation.surface: A diet that makes you less rigid.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet cutting carbohydrate foods such as bread and potatoes is low in starch.

clue.text: Wealth, nothing more than material?

parts.note: wealth in ready money is cash
something that is nothing more than a thing is a mere thing

explanation.surface: Is wealth nothing more than materialism?
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is a fine soft wool fabric from the Kashmir goat.

clue.text: Quartet appearing in sensual revelry

indicators.note: appearing in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: sensual pleasures of the flesh are carnal
a quartet is four, IV in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A string quartet turns up at a sensual party.
explanation.definitionFit: A carnival is a festival of public merrymaking and partying.

clue.text: What prolific artist may do to make random selection

definitions.meaning: an artist who is prolific sketches many pictures
to choose by chance, for example from straws or slips

explanation.surface: A busy artist picks at random.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing straws or slips by chance decides a matter randomly.

clue.text: One entertaining the Spanish in residence

parts.note: one who entertains guests is a host
the Spanish word for the is el

explanation.surface: A host entertains Spanish guests at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostel is a cheap lodging house where travellers stay.

clue.text: Go out of one's way to entertain

definitions.meaning: to turn aside from a set course or route

explanation.surface: Going out of one's way to put on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Divert means to turn aside from a route, and also to amuse.

clue.text: Beer wasted cooking offal

indicators.note: cooking hints at letters mixed up like ingredients in a pan

explanation.surface: Wasted beer goes into the offal being cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetbread is a gland, the thymus or pancreas, eaten as meat.

clue.text: Doctor lets us scrap

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, mixing the letters around

explanation.surface: A medic lets two of us have a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a fight or scuffle, as is a tussle.

clue.text: Smooth tongue

definitions.meaning: to rub something until shiny and smooth

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: To polish is to make smooth; Polish is also the national language of Poland.

clue.text: Record pile should be organised, one believes

parts.note: a vinyl record is a disc

indicators.note: organised means put into a fresh order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A pile of records needs sorting, according to a believer.
explanation.definitionFit: A disciple is a follower who believes in a teacher's doctrine.

clue.text: Info turned up at short notice

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means reading the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: a notice in the paper is an advertisement, shortened to ad

explanation.surface: Information arrives at short notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses AT followed by AD, giving DA then TA.
explanation.definitionFit: Info is short for information, as are facts and figures.

clue.text: Good man, Leonard — he's living within a distant island

indicators.note: living within places this piece inside the others

parts.note: a good man is a saint, abbreviated ST
Len is a common short form of the name Leonard
taken as he, the 's being the verb is

explanation.surface: A good man called Leonard lives on a remote island.
explanation.walkthrough: St Helena is the remote South Atlantic island where Napoleon was exiled.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Helena is a far-flung British territory in the South Atlantic.

clue.text: Sign worker's put inside shelter

indicators.note: put inside places one piece within another

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
a worker ant, the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: A signwriter's worker is put up in a shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shed or roof propped against a wall.

clue.text: Notwithstanding lacking in variety

explanation.surface: Notwithstanding a lack of variety.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means nevertheless, and literally means identical in every case.
